title: Are plant-based substitutes healthier than meat?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: opinion which is based on your initial feelings or instinct and cannot be explained logically

keywords.term: as far as I am concerned
keywords.def: (phrase) used to indicate that you are giving your own opinion
look or be similar to something
(slang) a vegetarian – a person who doesn't eat meat
used to say that someone has been or done a particular thing for many years

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 您好，这里是BBC英语教学的《6分钟英语》。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Georgie. If you've heard about Meat-Free Mondays or Veganuary, you probably know about a trend which an increasing number of people are trying – to reduce, or even stop, eating meat.
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔。我是乔治。如果你听说过“无肉星期一”或“素食月”，你大概知道这样一个趋势：越来越多的人正在尝试减少甚至停止吃肉。

sentences.en: This is often for health, animal welfare or environmental reasons.
sentences.zh: 这通常是为了健康、动物福利或环保的原因。

sentences.en: Instead, people are getting their daily amount of protein through plant-based alternatives – meat-free sausages and burgers made using ingredients like soy, tofu or fungi, as well as tempeh, beans or nuts.
sentences.zh: 相反，人们通过植物性替代品来获取每日所需的蛋白质——用大豆、豆腐、真菌以及豆豉、豆类或坚果等成分做成的无肉香肠和汉堡。

sentences.en: Have you tried any of these plant-based meat alternatives, Georgie?
sentences.zh: 乔治，你尝试过这些植物肉替代品吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I have. I have lots of vegetarian friends, so I've been to veggie barbecues, and have tried the plant-based sausages and burgers.
sentences.zh: 是的，我试过。我有很多素食朋友，所以我去过素食烧烤派对，也尝过植物香肠和汉堡。

sentences.en: I quite like them as long as they're covered in sauce.
sentences.zh: 只要上面浇了酱汁，我其实还挺喜欢的。

sentences.en: What about you? Yeah, I think I agree. They're fine.
sentences.zh: 你呢？是的，我想我同意。它们挺不错的。

sentences.en: There's a reason for them, but I'm not sure they're as good as the real thing.
sentences.zh: 它们存在是有原因的，但我不太确定它们是否和真肉一样好。

sentences.en: Now, with processed meat being linked to diseases like diabetes and cancer, most doctors agree that plant-based options are healthier.
sentences.zh: 如今，由于加工肉类与糖尿病和癌症等疾病有关，大多数医生都同意植物性选择更健康。

sentences.en: But some people are worried about how plant-based alternatives are made, including radio listener, Graham Glover, who asked this question to BBC Radio 4 programme, Sliced Bread: Well, my question is – looking at these vegetable sausages, how they are processed, full of additives and flavourings and colourings – are they any healthier than a pork sausage?
sentences.zh: 但有些人担心植物替代品的制作过程，其中包括BBC Radio 4节目《Sliced Bread》的听众格雷厄姆·格洛弗，他向该节目提出了这样一个问题：“我的问题是——看看这些蔬菜香肠，它们是怎么加工的，充满了添加剂、调味剂和色素——它们比猪肉香肠更健康吗？”

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll be finding out whether plant-based foods really are a healthier alternative to meat.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将探讨植物性食品是否真的是比肉类更健康的替代品。

sentences.en: And as usual, we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 像往常一样，我们将学习一些实用的新词汇和短语。

sentences.en: Remember, you can find all the vocabulary, along with a quiz and a worksheet, on our website bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到所有的词汇，以及小测试和练习页。

sentences.en: But now I have a question for you, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 但现在我有一个问题要问你，乔治。

sentences.en: Listener Graham loves eating sausages, but do you know which of the following words means 'sausages' in British English slang?
sentences.zh: 听众格雷厄姆喜欢吃香肠，你知道以下哪个词在英式英语俚语中是“香肠”的意思吗？

sentences.en: Is it: a) booze, b) banger, or c) brunch?
sentences.zh: 是：a) booze，b) banger，还是 c) brunch？

sentences.en: So, I actually know the answer to this question, so I'm not going to say.
sentences.zh: 其实我知道这个问题的答案，所以我不打算说。

sentences.en: Otherwise, it will spoil it for our listeners.
sentences.zh: 否则，这会剧透给我们的听众。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll all find out at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。嗯，我们都会在节目结束时揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Although most research agrees that plant-based foods are healthier than meat, it's also true that meat-free products are processed.
sentences.zh: 虽然大多数研究一致认为植物性食品比肉类更健康，但无肉产品也是经过加工的，这也是事实。

sentences.en: To make meat-free sausages, for example, after the proteins are broken down, flavourings and colourings are added to reproduce the taste or texture of meat.
sentences.zh: 例如，为了制作无肉香肠，在蛋白质被分解后，会添加调味剂和色素来重现肉类的口感或质地。

sentences.en: Quorn, one of the best-known brands of meat-free products, uses mycoprotein, a fungi-based protein similar to the fungi used in the fermentation of yoghurt and bread.
sentences.zh: Quorn 是最著名的无肉产品品牌之一，它使用的是真菌蛋白，这是一种类似于用来发酵酸奶和面包的真菌的基于真菌的蛋白质。

sentences.en: So, what does listener Graham think? Let's find out as he talks to Greg Foot, presenter of BBC Radio 4's Sliced Bread: Graham, listening to all this, you know, normally a fan of a meat sausage – you're plant-based, meat-alternative sausage curious, that we're exploring today – what do you think about hearing about the sources of where they come from?
sentences.zh: 那么，听众格雷厄姆是怎么想的呢？让我们听听他与BBC Radio 4节目《Sliced Bread》的主持人格雷格·福特的对话来了解一下：“格雷厄姆，听了这些，你知道的，你通常是肉香肠的粉丝——对于我们今天正在探索的植物性、肉类替代香肠，你觉得听到它们的来源怎么想？”

sentences.en: What's your gut reaction to hearing that Quorn comes from a fungus?
sentences.zh: 听到 Quorn 来自真菌，你第一直觉是什么？

sentences.en: I have no problems with that… it's just another form of protein, as far as I'm concerned – it's what's the healthiest.
sentences.zh: 我对此没有问题……在我看来，它只是另一种形式的蛋白质——什么最健康才是关键。

sentences.en: Yes, we will get to health. I think that's the big conversation for today.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们会谈到健康。我认为这是今天的主要话题。

sentences.en: Greg asks Graham for his gut reaction. Your gut reaction is your opinion based on your initial feeling or instinct about something.
sentences.zh: 格雷格问格雷厄姆的第一直觉是什么。你的直觉是根据你对某事物的最初感觉或本能得出的看法。

sentences.en: It can't be explained logically. Actually, Graham doesn't mind that his sausage protein is a fungus, as long as it's healthy.
sentences.zh: 这无法从逻辑上解释。实际上，格雷厄姆并不介意他的香肠蛋白质是真菌，只要它健康就行。

sentences.en: He uses the phrase, as far as I am concerned, to indicate that he is giving his own opinion on the subject.
sentences.zh: 他用“就我而言”这个短语来表明他对这个主题表达自己的看法。

sentences.en: Of course, healthy eating is important, but there are other factors influencing whether meat lovers like Graham could be persuaded to try plant-based alternatives.
sentences.zh: 当然，健康饮食很重要，但还有其他因素影响着像格雷厄姆这样的肉食爱好者是否会被说服去尝试植物性替代品。

sentences.en: These include things like the taste, colour and texture of the sausage – in other words, whether a plant-based sausage looks and feels like real meat.
sentences.zh: 这些因素包括香肠的味道、颜色和质地——换句话说，植物香肠看起来和摸起来是否像真正的肉。

sentences.en: Here's Greg discussing this point for BBC Radio 4 programme, Sliced Bread: It's interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 以下是格雷格为BBC Radio 4节目《Sliced Bread》讨论这一点：“这很有趣，不是吗？”

sentences.en: Because my mum is a long-time veggie, and we were talking about this, and she says, "I don't want my, you know, alternative proteins to resemble meat." That's one of the reasons she says she doesn't eat meat.
sentences.zh: 因为我妈妈是个老素食主义者，我们讨论过这个，她说：‘我不想让我的，你知道的，替代蛋白质像肉。’这就是她说她不吃肉的原因之一。

sentences.en: But you, Graham, you said you do want your plant-based sausage to resemble a pork sausage.
sentences.zh: 但你，格雷厄姆，你说你确实希望你的植物香肠像猪肉香肠。

sentences.en: Yeah, I've always been a meat eater, but I do need a plant-based product to be similar in terms of flavour, texture, and appearance.
sentences.zh: 是的，我一直是个肉食者，但我确实需要一个在风味、质地和外观上都相似的植物产品。

sentences.en: Graham wants his plant-based sausages to resemble, meaning look similar to, meat.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆希望他的植物香肠 resemble（类似），也就是看起来像肉。

sentences.en: But that's not the case for Greg's mum, who's a long-time veggie.
sentences.zh: 但格雷格的妈妈并非如此，她是一个老素食主义者。

sentences.en: A veggie is slang for a vegetarian, a person who doesn't eat meat.
sentences.zh: veggie 是 vegetarian 的俚语，指不吃肉的人。

sentences.en: And the adjective long-time describes someone who has been or done a particular thing for many years.
sentences.zh: 形容词 long-time（长期的）描述某人做某事或成为某种状态已经很多年了。

sentences.en: So, a long-time veggie is someone who's been vegetarian for many years.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个 long-time veggie 就是吃素很多年的人。

sentences.en: Whether you want your veggie sausages to look, taste and feel like meat, or you prefer your protein from a plant, now there's every chance you'll find what you're looking for… …and keep your body, and planet, healthy as well.
sentences.zh: 无论你是希望你的素香肠看起来、尝起来和摸起来都像肉，还是更喜欢植物蛋白，现在你很有可能会找到你正在寻找的东西…………同时保持身体和地球的健康。

sentences.en: Now, isn't it time you revealed the answer to your question, Neil?
sentences.zh: 尼尔，现在是不是该公布你那个问题的答案了？

sentences.en: Yes, I asked what the British English slang word for sausages is.
sentences.zh: 是的，我问过英式英语中香肠的俚语是什么。

sentences.en: And what is it, Georgie? The answer is banger.
sentences.zh: 是什么呢，乔治？答案是 banger。

sentences.en: And we have a typical dish in the UK called bangers and mash, which is sausages and mash.
sentences.zh: 我们在英国有一道典型的菜叫 bangers and mash，也就是香肠土豆泥。

sentences.en: Mmm, love it – with gravy! OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with banger, a word which is slang for sausage.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我喜欢——配上肉汁！好的。让我们回顾一下我们学过的词汇，从 banger 开始，这是一个意思是香肠的俚语。

sentences.en: Your gut reaction is your opinion about something, based on instinctive feelings, not logic or reason.
sentences.zh: 你的直觉是你对某事的看法，基于本能的感觉，而不是逻辑或理性。

sentences.en: The phrase, as far as I am concerned, can be used to give your opinion about something.
sentences.zh: 短语“就我而言”可以用来表达你对某事的看法。

sentences.en: To resemble means to look or be similar to something.
sentences.zh: resemble 的意思是看起来或类似于某物。

sentences.en: A veggie is slang for a vegetarian – someone who doesn't eat meat.
sentences.zh: veggie 是 vegetarian 的俚语——指不吃肉的人。

sentences.en: And finally, the adjective long-time can be used to say that someone has done a particular thing for many years.
sentences.zh: 最后，形容词 long-time 可以用来表示某人做某事已经很多年了。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember you can find worksheets, quizzes and loads more resources to improve your English over on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了，但请记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到练习页、小测试和更多提升英语水平的资源。

sentences.en: See you there soon, but for now, goodbye!
sentences.zh: 很快在那里见，但现在，再见！

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
